title:
Base type for a result object returned from a method. Result objects have additional validation when returned by
method call, see {@link ValidateObjSpec}.

Result-specific validation requires all mandatory fields to have values. If an object embedded within a result
object is also a result, it is also verified. This allows the caller of a method that results a result to know
that the result will be "complete".

This means that code which receives an instance of a **Result** knows that all fields will have values as
specified by the type (required fields will be non-null, etc), so it can avoid extra checks and just use
the fields as one would expect.

In other words: result-specific validation ensures that all mandatory fields in a Result object have values. If a
Result object contains another Result object, the embedded object is also validated. This guarantees that the entire
Result object is complete, meaning all required fields are populated.

Note that non-Result instances are not guaranteed to be complete, because they need to be passed around while being
set up.

For example, {@link Obj#make make} must be able return an Obj that is incomplete or invalid because the caller may
want to build it up in stages.
